scope: Alpine Linux 64-bit only: amd64 and arm64.

new_draft_prs.baseline: arm64 pthread_attr_t reports 8 bytes; C reports 56 bytes.
Native csize_t outputs fail Nim checking; detach-state output is passed by value.

new_draft_prs.purpose: Correct Linux arm64 scalar widths and signedness
new_draft_prs.baseline: ClockId and nine other scalar typedefs report 8 bytes instead of native 4 bytes.

new_draft_prs.purpose: Match the C representation of opaque iconv handles
new_draft_prs.baseline: Clang C++ rejects assigning iconv_open's void pointer to a generated struct pointer.

themes.theme: Missing GNU extensions, headers and include-order assumptions
themes.result: No listed dependency found in lib/compiler; focused fixtures compile with GCC and Clang.
Process spawning, descriptor flags and name/page limits pass. No listed obsolete aliases found.
Core fixtures build on musl without a __MUSL__ macro. Linux iconv detection needed the existing header fix.

themes.theme: Large-file interfaces, native types and conflicting headers
themes.result: 5 GiB sparse offsets pass. Native-size probes exposed incorrect pthread structs and arm64 scalar types; their fixes pass.

themes.theme: strerror_r and other incorrect C signatures
themes.result: The POSIX strerror_r wrapper matches Nim error messages. Pthread attribute getters needed four corrected output signatures.

themes.theme: Dependencies built against the wrong libc
themes.result: A musl-built plugin loads; a glibc-built plugin needing gnu_get_libc_version is rejected. Static PCRE works with its static package and override.
A Nim-created worker fills and reads a 512 KiB local array. C/C++, ORC/refc and sanitizer probes pass.

themes.theme: stdio, opaque FILE, printf rounding and EOF
themes.result: EOF resets, descriptor redirection and rounding pass. Direct stdout assignment is an expected musl compile rejection. FILE repr uses the existing compiler fix.
Nim Unicode casing, numeric parsing and formatting pass. Libc German collation remains bytewise, an expected limitation.

themes.theme: iconv coverage, substitution, BOM and handle types
themes.result: Supported conversions and UTF-16/32 BOMs pass. ASCII substitution, unsupported //TRANSLIT and GBK output are verified libc behavior. Static binding and C++ handle fixes pass.
Nim parseopt handles options after a positional argument. Raw libc getopt stops there, as expected.

themes.theme: Dynamic linker, lazy binding and plugin unloading
themes.result: Symbol lookup, missing libraries, wrong-libc rejection and persistent state after dlclose pass. A fully static executable cannot load the shared plugin.

themes.theme: DNS, search domains, TCP fallback and NSS
themes.result: An isolated resolver verifies search expansion and a real TCP retry. Local root passwd/group lookups pass. Raw socket lookups use the existing nil-service fix.
Native getutent returns no records. Nim complex abs/sqrt and gamma smoke tests pass.
Clang ASan+UBSan pass for a C control and Nim file-I/O/thread-stack probes on both architectures. GCC runtime linking fails for the C control too; this is toolchain packaging.

additional_control: Debian glibc arm64 passes scalar and pthread-attribute regressions with C and C++.
additional_regression: Existing SSL socket regression passes the full two-architecture/compiler/backend/memory-manager matrix with PR #8 applied.

reproduce.command: bash tools/alpine/bootstrap.sh && python3 tools/alpine/run.py bin/nim --foreign bin/audit-foreign.so
reproduce.foreign_dependency: Build tools/alpine/foreign.c as a shared library on a glibc host; Alpine cannot build that intentionally incompatible control.
reproduce.ci: New PRs inherit the standard Alpine CI. The separate Alpine compatibility audit workflow bootstraps the combined branch, runs focused probes, and uploads logs/results.

limits: Focused regression probes do not prove every Nim function or third-party package works.
DNS probes cover a controlled IPv4 resolver, search domains and TCP fallback; arbitrary split-DNS/NSS deployments were not reproduced.
Locale/iconv and raw libc stubs are tested behavior, not promises of glibc feature parity.
